text:
Submarine God, lake God, river God,

one in the triton and the heron

and in the gentle corvette and the rough cruiser,

God of water, Lord of the Crystal House,

Sailor God.

Expression of water in your thousand expressions,

river stretched from Volturno to Christ,

flight of the ibis that crosses

from the figurehead of the Argo

to the mast of the Santa Maria, Argonaut God,

who extends to the hands of Harmony

the river of your music, long as a flute.

God infused in the white lake of the cloud

bordered in blue,

God of foam in the lamb's curl,

storm God in the lion's mane,

God the diviner, stilled in the tiger's pupil,

God of the river of stars that from East to West

crosses the sky at night,

God of the combatant water

in the maned Niagara and the suspicious Dardanelles:


Extend your right hand where the River is born

and your left where it empties

—in a crystal arch of Brahma—

extend the amphora of your hands,

Lord of Water, Old Commander,

toward the sonorous springs,

toward the warm still pool

of the belligerent-water Orinoco,

sprung from your temples, sweated from your pores

on the Saturday of your first rest!

translation.title: Invocation to the God of Waters
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the long invocation’s catalog of water forms, mythic vessels, rivers, and the final Orinoco image.
